reasoning: GeoNames 4007229 is the old silver camp of El Tigre in the Sierra El Tigre, which Silver Tiger Metals' history puts about 90 km south-south-east of Agua Prieta above the Bavispe; this point is 87 km from Agua Prieta and 27 km south of Colonia Morelos (straight-line), so a week's ride from the Pilares Teras fits. The other 14 El Tigre villages in Sonora and Chihuahua are farms or ranchos far from the Bavispe country and no mining town.

GeoNames 4015316 is the only Llanos de Carretas (feature PLN). It lies east of the Bavispe, 72 km straight-line north-east of Bavispe town and 48 km north-east of the old Hacienda Carretas (GeoNames 4015318), so it fits the view east over the Bavispe barranca from the Sonoran sierras. The coordinate is rounded to the half degree and the plain is an area, so treat it as a label point, or draw the plain as an area if one is made.

No gazetteer (GeoNames, Wikidata) or web source has the name, so it is probably invented or a lost name. The text puts it on the far (east) bank of the upper Bavispe at a ford, below a wagon road that drops east off the sierra, and several days of fording upriver (south) of Tamichopa. The estimate is the midpoint of the river reach between Mesa Tres Ríos and Huachinera, about 28 km straight-line south of Tamichopa; a local history naming a ruined mission town on that reach would settle it.

GeoNames 4017239 is the municipal seat (Wikidata Q2919569 agrees within 50 m), 14 km straight-line north of Bacerac on the river road, as in 2-03, and the town the 1887 earthquake destroyed. GeoNames 4017240, 14 km to the south-east, is a rounded point with no population and not the town.

GeoNames 3982557 (Wikidata Q61295693 agrees) is the old mission site on the upper Bavispe, 10 km straight-line south of Bacerac, which fits Billy passing it on the way downriver to Bacerac the same day. It is the only populated place of the name.
GeoNames 4017806 is the municipal seat (Wikidata Q2991325), on the river between Tamichopa (10 km south) and Bavispe (14 km north), straight-line, as the text orders them. No other namesake.

The text says Ojito, a roadside hamlet on the road north from Colonia Morelos toward the border (2-03), reached by the brothers the evening before they pass Morelos after midnight (2-07). GeoNames 3990426 El Ojito is 7 km straight-line north of Colonia Morelos, which fits both; the gazetteer's pick, a spring in Cibola County NM, is wrong, Ojitos in Chihuahua is 66 km east across the mountains, and Rancho El Ojito near the border is 51 km from Morelos, too far for an evening ride.

GNIS 4069, Douglas in Cochise County, the only US namesake and the border town facing Agua Prieta where the brothers halt at the gateshack (2-07). The Wikidata port-of-entry point (Q5301214) is about 1 km southwest, at the crossing itself, if a gate point is wanted.

No gazetteer has an Animas Plain; the text uses it for the open grassland floor of the southern Animas Valley (where the wolf runs antelope below the Peloncillos in 1-04, the view east from the Guadalupe pass in 2-04, and Billy's camp after the Sanders ranch in 4-02). Merge it into the existing animas-valley seed as an alt name (Animas Plain, Animas Plains) and draw the J3 and J7 stops as approximate points on the valley floor near Cloverdale, not a separate pin.

No GNIS or web source names an SK Bar ranch, and the gazetteer's only candidate, Sanders Ranch Cemetery in Cochise County, Arizona (Q117602497), is 68 km straight-line northwest of Cloverdale across the Peloncillos, so it is rejected. The text puts it nine miles north of the Parham house by road (1-02, 2-04) and on the road south from Animas (4-01); the estimate is about 14.5 km north of Cloverdale (GNIS 920578) on the Animas Valley road, which assumes the house is near Cloverdale. Draw it as an inferred circle of a few km; a historical brand or land record for a Sanders ranch in the valley would settle it.

GNIS 899504, Animas Peak in the Animas Mountains, Hidalgo County: 23 km straight-line northeast of Cloverdale and 58 km southwest of Hachita, matching the text's view from Hachita toward the southwest (4-08). The Sierra County Animas Peak (GNIS 885763) is 139 km northeast of Hachita in the Black Range and does not fit.
GNIS 891335, Lordsburg, Hidalgo County seat, where the sheriff's office is; the only namesake.

GNIS 10858 pins the valley in Graham County, 54 km straight-line north of Bowie, far from where the brothers enter it after crossing the low range west of the state line and noon at the river (2-07). Draw the valley as an area or label, and make the stop an approximate point on the San Simon River between the state line and San Simon town (GNIS 10856, 32.26786, -109.22756), which is 25 km east of Bowie.

GNIS 1890, Bowie in Cochise County; they cross the highway just east of it before taking the old road south through the Dos Cabezas (2-07). Apache Pass is 19 km straight-line south, which fits an evening crossing and a pass the next day.
GNIS 4038, the Dos Cabezas Mountains range point in Cochise County, south of Bowie on the brothers' route to Apache Pass. The Sonora Dos Cabezas places (GeoNames 3971320) are a different place.

GNIS 732, Apache Pass in Cochise County between the Dos Cabezas and Chiricahua Mountains, 19 km straight-line south of Bowie. The Santa Cruz County Apache Pass (GNIS 25713) is 185 km southwest and off the route.

The valley runs about 150 km from Willcox to Douglas; GNIS 11943 pins its south end 4 km from Douglas and Wikidata Q7636559 its north end, 96 km north of Elfrida, so neither point represents it. The brothers come down it from Apache Pass to route 666 and Elfrida (2-07); draw it as an area or a label placed between Elfrida and the Apache Pass foot.
GNIS 4408, Elfrida in Cochise County on the old route 666 down the Sulphur Springs Valley; the only namesake.
GNIS 7855, McNeal in Cochise County, on the same highway south of Elfrida toward Douglas; the only namesake.

GeoNames 4003756 agrees with Wikidata Q4228432 to about 0.1 km; it is the only Colonia Juárez in the region, 14 km straight-line south-west of Casas Grandes, which fits the ride to the ruins and Casas Grandes that evening. In reality the river at Colonia Juárez is the Piedras Verdes, though the text calls the river at the plank bridge the Casas Grandes.

GeoNames 4015075 and Wikidata Q35352850 put the river at its mouth near Laguna de Guzmán, 129 km straight-line north-north-east of San Diego, far from where the story uses it (the bridge at Colonia Juárez, the bridge below San Diego, and Billy's trail north past Corralitos). Draw the river as a line, including its upper course (the Palanganas past Mata Ortiz); make the crossings stops.

The gazetteer's pick (GeoNames 12193954, 28.68,-106.13) is near Chihuahua city, about 240 km away, and is wrong. Wikidata Q853265 (Casas Grandes archaeological site) sits beside Casas Grandes town (GeoNames 4015076, under 1 km), which matches the walled ruins passed on the road from Colonia Juárez to Casas Grandes.

San José Babícora (GeoNames 3986261, Gómez Farías municipio) is the Hacienda de San José de Babícora that Hearst-era photographs in the Bancroft Library (UC Berkeley digital collections) show as the ranch headquarters. It lies 13 km straight-line south-east of Laguna de Babícora and 12 km south-south-west of La Boquilla, on Billy's way from Boquilla to Santa Ana. The ranch itself covered about 360,000 ha (INAH Gaceta 2021), so per plan 2.4 draw it as a region; this point marks only the headquarters. Other Babícoras (Babícora de Conoachic, 28.71,-108.21) are outside the ranch country of the text.

The gazetteer's pick (San Diego del Monte, 28.65,-107.05) is wrong. GeoNames 3987333 (Colonia San Diego, Casas Grandes municipio) matches OpenStreetMap's Ex Hacienda de San Diego (30.24443,-108.00978) within 0.1 km. It is 16 km straight-line south-south-west of Casas Grandes and 7 km north of Mata Ortiz on the road south, with the Casas Grandes (Palanganas) and Piedras Verdes rivers below it, as the text describes.

GeoNames 3992608 is the Río Piedras Verdes near its junction with the Palanganas, 3 km straight-line north-west of the Hacienda de San Diego and 6 km south-east of Colonia Juárez. The story only sees it from the hacienda, so this single point is a fair place for it; if rivers are drawn as lines, draw it upstream through Colonia Juárez instead.

The gazetteer's pick (GeoNames 3999149, 29.73,-107.44) is a different Las Varas, 79 km south-east of San Diego and off the railroad. GeoNames 4006519, Las Varas (Estación Babícora), Madera municipio, agrees with Wikidata Q20215019 and with GeoNames 3999157. It is on the Ferrocarril Noroeste line 77 km straight-line due south of Mata Ortiz and 32 km west-north-west of La Boquilla, which fits the railroad town, the Madera road south and the road east to Boquilla.

GeoNames 3975330 (Juan Mata Ortiz) agrees with Wikidata Q4284456 within 0.2 km; the gazetteer's pick 3996407 is a rounded duplicate about 1.5 km off. It is 7 km straight-line south of the Hacienda de San Diego, the first town on the road south to Las Varas.

No gazetteer point exists for the plains; the only candidate is the lake (Laguna de Babícora, GeoNames 4017246), which the text treats separately. Draw the high plains as an area around the lake between Las Varas, La Boquilla, San José Babícora and Santa Ana, and use the lake point as a label anchor if needed.

No gazetteer point exists. In the text the valley lies on the wagon road to Namiquipa and below the juniper plain at La Pinta, so it is the upper Santa María valley between Santa Ana de Babícora and Namiquipa. Draw it as an area along the upper river there. GeoNames Valle Buenaventura (3987499) is a different, downstream valley.

GeoNames 3995134 agrees with Wikidata Q863021 to under 0.5 km; it is the only Namiquipa, the municipal seat on the upper Santa María, 25 km straight-line north-north-east of Santa Ana de Babícora. The text says Billy takes the road west from Santa Ana to Namiquipa, but the real town is to the north.

The gazetteer's pick, Boquilla y Anexas in Guerrero municipio (GeoNames 3976048, the INEGI locality the plan names), is 135 km straight-line south-east of Las Varas and nowhere near the lake, so it does not fit. GeoNames 8749710, La Boquilla in Gómez Farías municipio, is 32 km east-south-east of Las Varas and 10 km east of Laguna de Babícora, on the route Boquilla to La Pinta (15 km) to Santa Ana (44 km), matching the road east from Las Varas by the lake and the road south to Santa Ana. It sits 2 km east of the town of Valentín Gómez Farías; I found no source confirming the name Boquilla y Anexas there.

GeoNames 3984699 (Santa Ana, alternate name Santa Ana Babícora, Namiquipa municipio) is the only match, with the Santa Ana de Bavicora airfield (3984695) beside it. It is 44 km straight-line south-south-east of La Boquilla with La Pinta between them, as the text has it.

In the text the brothers leave the road north of Boquilla, ride west and then north through the night, and reach San José by following a river north; after the shooting Billy flees north to Mata Ortiz. San José de Ermita (GeoNames 3974647, Ignacio Zaragoza municipio, duplicated as 3986374) is on the upper Casas Grandes drainage 48 km straight-line north-north-west of La Boquilla and 48 km south of Mata Ortiz, which fits. The gazetteer's pick (3986371, 30.44,-107.95) is north of Casas Grandes, and San José 3986377 is only 4 km from Boquilla; neither fits. Many San Josés exist, so this remains a best fit.

GeoNames 3975183 (Madera municipio, matching Wikidata Q49979501; Ejido La Norteña 4011547 is a near duplicate) lies in the sierras 45 km straight-line west-north-west of Las Varas and 110 km west of Namiquipa. That fits a wagon road from La Norteña in the western sierras across the Babícora plains to Namiquipa, and Billy's ride west as far as the watershed.

GeoNames 4000793 (Gómez Farías municipio, with the La Pinta airfield 4000797 beside it) lies 15 km straight-line south-south-east of La Boquilla and 29 km north-west of Santa Ana de Babícora, exactly on Billy's road south between them. The other La Pinta nearby (8772006) is a stream.

The gazetteer's pick (GeoNames 3984097) is the river's mouth at Laguna de Santa María, 227 km straight-line north of Santa Ana; the other point (3984098) is mid-course, 26 km north of Namiquipa. The story uses headwater streams on the road from Santa Ana to Namiquipa (3-12) and the watershed north of San Buenaventura (4-06). Draw the river as a line and mark Billy's camp as a stop.

GeoNames 4012406, the city of Cuauhtémoc (municipal seat), is the only Cuauhtémoc in the region; it lies 108 km straight-line south-south-east of Namiquipa, the southern end of Billy's search. The town took the name in 1927, before the story's time.

GeoNames 4016722 is San Buenaventura, the municipal seat of Buenaventura on the Santa María; no other town of the name is in the region. It is 33 km straight-line south-south-east of Galeana, and the old road toward Gallego runs from it, as in 4-06.

Best estimate: Álamo, GeoNames 4018952 (Ignacio Zaragoza municipio, rounded coordinates), 15 km straight-line south-west of San Buenaventura and 41 km south of Galeana. El Álamo, GeoNames 4011228 (Buenaventura municipio), is 15 km north-east of San Buenaventura and 35 km from Galeana; neither lies between Buenaventura and Galeana as Billy rides north, and several Los Álamos are nearby too. A mid-century map (for example an AMS 1:250,000 sheet) showing which Álamo stood on the road north to Galeana would settle it.

GeoNames 3975370 (Hermenegildo Galeana, the municipal seat) is the only Galeana in the region, 33 km straight-line north-north-west of San Buenaventura on the way north to Casas Grandes, which fits both Billy's ride in 3-14 and Quijada's account in 4-05.

The gazetteer's pick (GeoNames 4011872, Dr. Belisario Domínguez) is 210 km south-south-east of San Buenaventura and does not fit. GeoNames 3985741, San Lorenzo in Buenaventura municipio, is 37 km straight-line east of San Buenaventura, where Boyd is buried, and 62 km south-east of Galeana. The other Chihuahua San Lorenzo near the story (9980175, Madera municipio) is 90 km from San Buenaventura. The text gives no direction, so this is the nearest fit rather than a certainty.
GNIS 897342, Columbus in Luna County, the border gate where Billy crosses north (4-01); 33 km straight-line south of the Florida Mountains point, which he passes the same evening.
GNIS 920596, the Florida Mountains range point in Luna County, between Columbus (33 km south) and Deming (21 km northwest), matching the ride north in 4-01.
GNIS 920584, Deming, Luna County seat, where the recruiting sergeant is; the only namesake on the route.

Wikidata Q16562, El Paso, Texas, reached by bus from Deming for the recruiting office (4-01). GNIS here covers only NM and AZ; the Sonora El Paso (GeoNames 3990407) is a ranch locality and irrelevant. It lies inside the story box, near its east edge.

GNIS 938832, Socorro, New Mexico, passed on the bus north to Albuquerque with the Rio Grande marshes beside the highway (4-01), and later the high plains west of it (4-02). The Chihuahua Socorro is a reservoir and does not fit.
GNIS 899669, Hermanas in Luna County, on the old road from Deming to Hachita; Hachita is 36 km straight-line west, matching the order in 4-01 and 4-08.
GNIS 920609, Hachita in Grant County (the book's Hatchita), with its crossroads store; Animas Peak lies 58 km to its southwest, as the text has it in 4-08.
GNIS 920632, the Little Hatchet Mountains range point, 15 km straight-line southwest of Hachita, where Billy rides through the foothills after leaving the road west of Hachita (4-01).

GNIS 920601, Gillespie Mountain in Hidalgo County, 13 km northeast of Animas Peak, so seen with the Animas Peaks beyond it from the Playas flats (4-01). The Graham County, Arizona, namesake (GNIS 5039) is 142 km northwest and does not fit.

GNIS 920562, the Big Hatchet Mountains in Hidalgo County, 23 km south-southeast of the Little Hatchets; the text's plain Hatchet Mountains, seen from the Animas Plain with Mexico beyond (4-02), most likely means the higher southern range, but could loosely mean both Hatchet ranges.

The Aztec Land and Cattle Company (the Hashknife) had its first headquarters across the Little Colorado from Joseph City and then at Holbrook (Wikipedia, Hashknife Outfit; Holbrook museum), but by Billy's time it was the Babbitt brothers' operation, as the Winslow barman says, and no source found gives its 1940s headquarters. The estimate is Holbrook (GNIS 5871), 51 km straight-line east of Winslow; better drawn as an inferred area on the Little Colorado between Winslow and Holbrook. A Babbitt-era ranch history would settle it.

Rivers are drawn as lines. GNIS 31050 pins the Little Colorado at its mouth in the Grand Canyon and the gazetteer pick (Q103403986) is a bridge 115 km northwest of Winslow, both far from the linecamp (4-02). The camp's site is not told; place it as an inferred area on the river near Winslow, where Billy collects his pay.

GNIS 13930, Winslow, Navajo County, Arizona. The text reads Window, but it has a post office and a First Street and is the town near a Hashknife linecamp on the Little Colorado, which fits Winslow; no place called Window exists in the area.
GNIS 908353, Magdalena in Socorro County, New Mexico, west of Socorro on the way to the plains of San Agustin (4-02); the Sonora and Chihuahua Magdalenas are hundreds of km south and do not fit.

GNIS 923769 (Area), the Plains of San Agustin in Catron County, the book's plains of Saint Augustine, crossed between Magdalena (97 km east-northeast of the point) and Silver City (123 km south). The basin is about 80 km long, so this is a label point; an area would be better.
GNIS 920706, Silver City, Grant County seat (Palace Hotel, Bullard Street); the only namesake.
GNIS 899927, Steins in Hidalgo County, 30 km straight-line west-southwest of Lordsburg on the old highway Billy crosses just east of it heading south to the SK Bar (4-02).

GeoNames 4010957 El Berrendo (PPL, Janos municipality) sits on the line at the Antelope Wells port of entry (Wikidata Q4771212, under 1 km away; GNIS 898517 Antelope Wells is 3 km NE), which is the Mexican customs post the text calls Berendo. The gazetteer's pick, the El Berrendo locality 4010955, is 82 km to the SE inland and has no crossing; the other dozen El Berrendos are farther south and east.

GeoNames 4004116, the municipal seat of Janos (PPLA2), 59 km SSE of the El Berrendo crossing (straight-line), which fits two days' ride south from the border with the western sierras in view. The other Janos points (two small Chihuahua places at 28.57 N and 28.27 N, and Los Janos in Sonora) are off the route.

GeoNames 3996956, the municipal seat Madera (Wikidata Q2447269 agrees within 1 km), a sawmill and railroad town as the text describes. The only other Madera town is in southern Sonora. The 3-01 Madero the troupe's men go to is the same place: the troupe is camped on the Madera road south of Las Varas.

GeoNames 3982082, the municipal seat Temósachic (Wikidata Q2455181 agrees), 40 km SE of Madera (straight-line), which fits the road south out of Madera toward it. GeoNames 3982081 puts a Temósachic in Sonora with rounded coordinates and is likely an error; Temosachi 3982083 is a different hamlet 36 km NW of Madera.

GeoNames 3994946 Sierra el Nido (alt Sierra del Nido), the only range of that name in Chihuahua. Its centre point is 73 km from San Buenaventura at a bearing of 116 degrees (straight-line), so ESE rather than due south as the text has it; the range is long and its high peaks may read as south from the cemetery road. A point is acceptable, but the range could be drawn as an area.

GeoNames 4012754 Corralitos (alt Hacienda Corralitos; Wikidata Q20144121, Nuevo Casas Grandes municipality), the old hacienda and smelter town 37 km due north of Casas Grandes (straight-line), which fits a night's ride north along the Casas Grandes River with slagheaps in view. Nuevo Corralitos 4012755 is the railway section 11 km SSE; 3975894 and 4012753 are bare rounded points; the other Corralitos are far south.

The gazetteer pick, GNIS 905803 Dog Springs in Socorro County, is 279 km straight-line north of Hermanas and is wrong: the text has Billy pass the first boundary obelisk west of Dog Springs and an old dry reservoir, on his way north from the Casas Grandes River, and ride through Hermanas the next day (4-08). No GNIS, GeoNames or web source found names a Dog Springs on the Luna County border; the estimate is the boundary (31 deg 47 min N) south of Hermanas. A boundary survey monument list or an old USGS sheet of the Hermanas area would settle it.
GNIS 4189, Duncan in Greenlee County, Arizona, west of Silver City on the Gila; the text names it Duncan Arizona, so there is no ambiguity.
GNIS 923604, Glenwood in Catron County, on the road north through the mountains from Duncan toward Reserve (4-08); the only namesake.
GNIS 923657, Reserve, Catron County seat, north of Glenwood (4-08); the only namesake.

No gazetteer entry or web source found for a GS ranch. The text only says Billy worked for the GS outfit while drifting between Silver City, Duncan, Glenwood and Reserve (4-08), so it is probably in the Gila or San Francisco River country, but no headquarters is known. Leave it off the map or as a note on that segment; a historical brand book for Grant or Catron County would settle it.

Two readings: the Carrizozo Cattle Company of Lincoln County, which named the town of Carrizozo (GNIS 918425, 33.64174, -105.87721), or a local outfit, since GNIS has a Carrizozo Canyon and Spring in Socorro County near Magdalena (GNIS 904810, 904812). The text names the Carrizozos alongside the GS while Billy works the Silver City, Glenwood and Reserve country (4-08), which fits neither well. A source tying a 1940s Carrizozo outfit to the Gila country would settle it.

GNIS 920698, Santa Rita (historical), the company town swallowed by the Chino open pit, on the old road east from Silver City: 21 km straight-line east of Silver City and 13 km west of San Lorenzo, matching the order in 4-08. The gazetteer pick (Q116713231) is a mine power station, and the Mexican Santa Ritas are irrelevant.
GNIS 920693, San Lorenzo in Grant County on the Mimbres, 13 km east of Santa Rita on the old road to the Black Range (4-08). The Chihuahua San Lorenzo where Boyd was killed is a separate seed.

GNIS 920566, the Black Range point in Grant County, 37 km north of San Lorenzo. Billy crosses the range on the old road east, which goes over Emory Pass (GNIS 906157, 32.91007, -107.76670); use the range point as a label and the pass for the route.

GNIS 920657, the Organ Mountains in Dona Ana County. The text sees them about eighty miles off from the plain east of the Black Range; Emory Pass to this point is 131 km (81 miles) straight-line, which fits.

GeoNames 4004887 Heroica Caborca (Wikidata Q1024929), the town with the old mission church whose ruined dome the heretic describes. Inside the story box at its western edge. The text puts it on the Altar River; strictly the town stands a little below where the Altar's lower course ends, 22 km straight-line to the east-south-east (GeoNames 4018697).

A tale river named only as Caborca's river. Its two gazetteer points (GeoNames 4030252 and 4018697) are 64 km and 22 km straight-line from Caborca, and neither marks anything in the story; draw the river as a line if at all, and let the Caborca point carry the tale.

GeoNames 4017288 Batepito, the settlement by the Batepito stream (GeoNames 4017287, 4 km west), 3 km straight-line from Colonia Morelos; this is the text's Batopite (2-01) and Part I's Batopito River. It is 45 km straight-line from Bavispe, a day's ride as the tale implies. The coordinate is rounded to the arc-minute, so it is good to about 1 to 2 km.

In the heretic's tale (2-01) the bereaved father wanders abroad, named in one breath with Guatemala, which suggests a Caribbean or Central American Trinidad (the island of Trinidad, or Trinidad in Cuba) rather than a local village, but the text gives no other clue. The gazetteer pick, a Trinidad in Sonora (GeoNames 3981010), is unsupported. It cannot be told; leave it unplaced or as a text-only tale mention.
GeoNames 3530597, Mexico City, the national capital; outside the story box. No ambiguity.

GeoNames 3971312 La Ramada lies 28 km straight-line east-south-east of Bacerac in the mountains toward Chihuahua, and Ciénega de Horcones (GeoNames 8881777) lies 7 km beyond it to the east, which matches the text's track east from Bacerac ending at Las Ramadas before the divide to Los Horcones (2-08). The spelling differs (singular), and the gazetteer's pick, a picnic ground near Phoenix, is wrong.

No Los Horcones lies across the divide east of Bacerac. Best estimate is GeoNames 8881777 Ciénega de Horcones (Sonora, pop. 95), 35 km ESE of Bacerac and 67 km WSW of Casas Grandes (straight-line), in the mountains on the way to the Chihuahua plains; the gazetteer's pick 8678297 is 11 km south of Bacerac in the Bavispe valley, on the wrong side of the divide, and Ciénega de Horcones in Chihuahua (3975924) is 127 km east. An old map of the Bacerac to Casas Grandes trail (with Las Ramadas) would settle it.

GeoNames 4011743, Victoria de Durango, capital of Durango state, where the opera troupe played and the blind man was jailed (3-01, 3-09); outside the story box. The gazetteer's picks (a Ciudad Juarez neighbourhood, a Chihuahua hamlet) are wrong.
GeoNames 3995523, Monclova, Coahuila, a city on the troupe's circuit named with Durango and Monterrey (3-01); outside the story box. Other Monclovas are small places in Campeche and Chiapas.
GeoNames 3995465, Monterrey, capital of Nuevo Leon, on the same circuit (3-01); outside the story box. The gazetteer pick is a Ciudad Juarez neighbourhood and wrong.

GeoNames 3995171 Naco, Sonora (Wikidata Q1963147), the border town where the cattle pens stood; Naco, Arizona (GNIS 8475) is 1 km straight-line across the line. The herd in 3-04 comes north out of Chihuahua, so the Mexican side is the natural point.

No La Quemada is known within the Babícora estate (Madera, Gómez Farías, Temósachic, Matachí and Namiquipa municipalities, per Vozenred 2015). Best estimate is GeoNames 4000530 Ejido La Quemada, in Cuauhtémoc municipality, 59 km SE of Namiquipa and 96 km SE of Laguna de Babícora (straight-line), which is south but likely outside the estate; Mesa Quemada 8752271 near Madera is a landform to the west, not south. A map of the Hearst Babícora divisions would settle it.

Open question (docs/open-questions.md). GeoNames 13416932 Nahuerachi (alt Nahuerachic) is a small locality in Madera municipio, 7 km south-south-west of Madera, inside the municipios the Babícora estate covered. The name differs from the text's Nahuerichic by one vowel, and no source yet ties the division to this place.

GeoNames 4004867, Hidalgo del Parral (PPLA2), 194 km SSE of Chihuahua city (straight-line), outside the story box. The gazetteer's pick 12193960 is a Parral neighbourhood inside Chihuahua city and is wrong.

GeoNames 4003797, Juan B. Ceballos, a village in Durango municipality 21 km straight-line north of Durango city on the road north; the blind man reaches it on his third day walking north from the Durango jail, then Rodeo after nine (3-09). Ceballos in Mapimi (GeoNames 4014938) is 282 km away, off the Parral road; outside the story box.

GeoNames 3988515, Rodeo, seat of Rodeo municipality, Durango, 129 km straight-line north of Durango city on the old road to Parral, and 122 km west of Torreon, matching the Huertistas marching east to Torreon (3-09); outside the story box. The gazetteer pick, Rodeo in Hidalgo County NM, is wrong.

GeoNames 3994097, Rio del Oro (Sestin), a Nazas headwater in Durango; the point is likely its lower end near the El Palmito reservoir, 67 km northwest of Rodeo. Rodeo itself stands on the Nazas below that confluence, so the book's Rodeo on the Rio Oro is loose; draw as a label or line, outside the story box.

GeoNames 3981254, Torreon, Coahuila, the Laguna city taken in the 1914 revolutionary battles that the blind man's tale and the drunk soldier refer to (3-09, 4-03); 122 km east of Rodeo. The New Mexico and Chihuahua Torreons are hamlets; outside the story box.

GeoNames 4014338, the state capital Chihuahua (PPLA; Wikidata Q61302 agrees within 2 km), where the blind man's tale puts the alameda. The other candidates are small Sonora places or urban colonias in Ciudad Juárez.

GeoNames 4013728, Ciudad Acuna, Coahuila, across from Del Rio, Texas, home of the border radio station XERA heard in the doctor's car (3-10); outside the story box. The gazetteer pick, a Sonora reservoir, is wrong.

Socorro Rivera and two companions were killed by Babícora guards in April 1939 at the paraje Las Varitas in the Alta Babícora near Madera (Vozenred 2015; Crónica de Chihuahua), but no source gives its location. Best estimate is GeoNames 8752482 Cerro las Varitas in Madera municipality, 23 km NW of Madera and 17 km W of the locality named Socorro Rivera (3974541); the gazetteer's pick 3999150 (alt Rancho Las Varas) is 88 km south near Guerrero, outside the estate. Agrarian records (RAN) for the Babícora would settle it.

Open question (docs/open-questions.md). INEGI (locality 080480065) and GeoNames 3984699 give Soto Máynez as the official name of Santa Ana de Babícora, so the two share this point. But in 3-12 girls are walking toward Soto Maynez after the riders have passed back through Santa Ana, as if it were a separate town. Shown as one place with both names until evidence settles it.

Wikidata Q65121339, Fort Bliss Main Post Historic District in El Paso, the 1940s post the sergeant names (4-01), 8 km from central El Paso. The GNIS Fort Bliss point in Otero County (GNIS 2512186) is the training range, 64 km away; inside the story box near its east edge.

Wikidata Q1297, Chicago; named only on a souvenir ashtray from the 1933 Century of Progress fair at Sanders' house (4-01), so it is a passing mention; outside the story box. Consider whether it should be mapped at all.

Wikidata Q981834, Matador, Motley County, Texas, the Matador Land and Cattle Company's home headquarters (Texas Historical Commission marker; Ranching Heritage Center's Matador office). The text puts Billy in the north panhandle, which may mean the company's Alamositas division in Oldham and Hartley counties instead; outside the story box.

No source found for a T Diamond ranch in the Texas panhandle in the 1940s; the only T Diamond found is a ranch near Hamlin on the Double Mountain Fork of the Brazos (land listings), well south of the panhandle the text names (4-02). Leave it unplaced; a Handbook of Texas or brand record would settle it.
Wikidata Q309172, Kwajalein Atoll, Marshall Islands, where Miller was killed (4-02, the 1944 battle); far outside the story box.
GNIS 894171, Roswell, Chaves County, New Mexico, where Leona now lives (4-02); just outside the story box to the east (-104.52).

GeoNames 4013708 Ciudad Juárez (PPLA2; Wikidata Q26590), the border city whose radio station the cook listens to. The other Juárez candidates are small places (Colonia Juárez, Juárez near Janos) without a broadcast station.

GeoNames 3979844, Zacatecas city, capital of Zacatecas state, scene of the 1914 battle where the drunk soldier took three bullets (4-03); outside the story box. The gazetteer pick, a Ciudad Juarez neighbourhood, is wrong.

GeoNames 3975344, the municipal seat Ignacio Zaragoza (PPLA2), 37 km SW of San Buenaventura (straight-line), where Boyd is buried, so a natural place for the rumour of his death. The other Chihuahua namesakes (3975343 near Janos, 141 km NW; El Willy 3975345; 4004419 near Cuauhtémoc) are smaller and farther from the story's events.
GeoNames 4017791, the municipal seat Bachíniva (Wikidata Q863131 agrees), the pueblo named in the corrido; the only namesake.

GeoNames 3975006 El Galleguito (alt Hacienda de Gallego), with the duplicate 4009777 and the El Gallego railway station 4006048 3 km west, 107 km due east (bearing 91 degrees) of San Buenaventura (straight-line), which fits the old road east out of town through a gap toward Gallego. No other Gallego exists in the region.

GeoNames 4005067 Sección Estación Guzmán, the railway settlement on the Juárez to Casas Grandes line, 75 km NE of Corralitos (straight-line), so a road coming down from Guzmán and Sabinal would cross Billy's route SE of Casas Grandes. The only other Guzmán is in Sonora; the text may mean the older Guzmán settlement or the Laguna de Guzmán area, which lie nearby.

GeoNames 3988340 Sabinal Viejo (alt El Sabinal, Rancho El Sabinal), the old settlement 39 km NE of Corralitos (straight-line) between it and Guzmán. Sabinal station (3988339) is 14 km east on the railway and would also fit; the Sabinal in New Mexico is far outside the area.

GeoNames 3991350 Puerto Palomas de Villa (Wikidata Q4384919 agrees within 1 km), the border town 6 km south of Columbus, New Mexico (straight-line). The gazetteer's pick, Palomas Viejo 3974803, is a hamlet 7 km SSE; the other Palomas are far south and not on the border.

GeoNames gives the Río Papigochic one Chihuahua point near Guerrero (3993466) and Wikidata/GeoNames 3993465 a point near the Yaqui in Sonora (29.17 N, 109.57 W), neither at the gorge where the gypsies lost the plane. Draw the river as a line from stage 2; the gorge is the Huápoca canyon reach west of Madera, where the Madera to Mesa Tres Ríos road bridges it.

GeoNames 4013362 Mesa Tres Ríos (Wikidata Q55668904, Nácori Chico municipality, Sonora), 91 km NW of Madera (straight-line), the end of the mountain road from Madera that crosses the Papigochic at Huápoca, which fits the bridge on the Mesa Tres Ríos road. The point marks the town the road is named for, not the bridge itself.

GeoNames 3988265 is the municipal seat (Wikidata Q20131758), where the gypsies come out of the mountains and wait for the truck (4-06); it is 18 km straight-line from Bacanora, the next stop. The other two Sahuaripas in GeoNames are hamlets near Hermosillo, off the route.

GeoNames 4011908 is the municipal seat (Wikidata Q3844435), 66 km straight-line north-north-west of Sahuaripa, so a truck coming down from it reaches Sahuaripa and goes on south-west to Bacanora. Divisadero near Cananea (270 km) and an unnamed Divisaderos south-west of Tónichi (108 km, the wrong side of the route) fit less well. The text only says the truck came from there, not that the gypsies went there.
GeoNames 4017826 is the municipal seat (Wikidata Q2652290), 18 km straight-line west-south-west of Sahuaripa and 45 km north of Tónichi, in route order. No other namesake.

GeoNames 3981363 Tónichi (Wikidata Q4460511), the town on the Río Yaqui in Soyopa municipality, 45 km straight-line south-south-west of Bacanora and 58 km north of Nuri, in route order. The gazetteer's pick, Rancho Tonichi near Ures, is 157 km off the route.

GeoNames 3994565 is the town of Nuri (population recorded), 58 km straight-line south-south-east of Tónichi, from where the text turns the route north to San Nicolás. GeoNames 3994566, 10 km to the south, is a rounded point with no population and probably a duplicate or outlying ranch.

GeoNames 3970707 San Nicolás, in Yécora municipality (Mindat lists a San Nicolás locality there), is 38 km straight-line north-north-east of Nuri and 26 km west of Yécora, exactly the text's leg north out of Nuri to San Nicolás and Yécora. GeoNames 3985266, 8 km south-west, is a rounded point that is probably the same place; the other 18 namesakes are far from the route.
GeoNames 3979954 is the municipal seat (Wikidata Q22874690), 26 km straight-line east of San Nicolás on the road over the mountains to Temósachic and Madera. No other namesake.

No Taliafero or Taliaferro ranch was found in any gazetteer or web source; it may be invented. Best estimate is the coordinates of Flores Magón (GeoNames 3988731), since the text puts it out of that town. A period land record or map of the Flores Magón colony would settle it.

GeoNames 3988731 Flores Magón (Wikidata Q49984203, Buenaventura municipality), the farming town 49 km ENE of San Buenaventura (straight-line), near the region of Billy's search. A second Flores Magón 8744544 is a small place 14 km west; the Ricardo Flores Magón entries are urban colonias in Chihuahua city, Delicias and Juárez.
Wikidata Q51698, McAllen, Hidalgo County, Texas, named by the man at the fire (4-07); outside the story box.

GNIS 923600, the village of Fort Sumner, De Baca County seat (the text's Fort Summer), where Billy looked for his sister's grave (4-07; his mother came from a De Baca County ranch). The old fort site (Q1514927) is 9 km southeast; the village is the better label; outside the story box.
